name: Level 2 Supervised Autonomous Code-Generation Agent
description: Turn AQT's existing planning, generation, tool, approval, and verification components into a real bounded coding agent. The agent may implement scoped code changes and repair them through real checks, while risky or final changes remain reviewable and human-supervised.

metadata.autonomyDefinition: The agent plans and implements a bounded task, executes configured tools and checks, performs limited repairs, records evidence, and requests approval before consequential actions.
nonGoals: No autonomous merge, release, deployment, or production changes
No reporting scaffold output or simulated verification as a successful implementation
No execution of commands or tools outside configured workspace and policy limits
metadata.prerequisiteAssessment: Builds on the existing WorkOrchestrator, AgentPlanner, ToolRegistry, CodeGenerator, verification-repair loop, API, CLI, and MCP integrations; replace current stubbed execution and verification paths with tested behavior.

existingModulesToReuse.src/agent/contracts.js: Untracked partial implementation of P12-T001 (task/plan/completion validation); not yet wired or tested
existingModulesToReuse.src/agent/workspace-context.js: Untracked partial implementation of P12-T004 (bounded, hashed, workspace-contained context); not yet wired or tested
existingModulesToReuse.src/agent/diff-review-system.js: Atomic writes, backups, and stale-source detection for P12-T006
existingModulesToReuse.src/agent/permissions.js: PermissionManager approval modes, protected paths, and dangerous-command rules for P12-T007
existingModulesToReuse.src/agent/verification-repair-loop.js: Verification result states and repair loop for P12-T008 and P12-T009
existingModulesToReuse.src/agent/privacy-cost-controls.js: BudgetManager and PrivacyManager for cost caps and redaction in P12-T002, P12-T009, and P12-T010
existingModulesToReuse.src/agent/provider-model-selector.js: Provider and model selection for P12-T002
existingModulesToReuse.src/agent/streaming-conversation.js: CancellationController and SessionPersistence for P12-T002 and P12-T010
existingModulesToReuse.src/agent/acceptance-workflow.js: Acceptance-criteria verification for P12-T001 and P12-T012
existingModulesToReuse.src/agent/requirement-traceability.js: Requirement-to-change traceability for P12-T010 and P12-T012

estimateRevision.reason: Reduced by 50 hours to account for reusing existing agent modules (contracts.js, workspace-context.js, diff-review-system.js, permissions.js, verification-repair-loop.js, privacy-cost-controls.js, provider-model-selector.js, streaming-conversation.js). Savings are limited because most of these modules have no tests yet; P12-T003 is unchanged because its added tool-hardening scope offsets reuse savings.

metadata.crossCheckNote: WorkOrchestrator currently uses none of the reuse modules above; its _checkPermissions, _executeStep, and _verifyWork are independent simplified or stubbed paths. As of P12-T003 (2026-10-07), ToolRegistry no longer exposes execute_command; it has a hash-guarded edit_file tool, an allowlisted run_check tool (checkId only), and get_diagnostics now runs real linter diagnostics (or reports unavailable with a reason). WorkOrchestrator now injects the ToolRegistry into step execution with per-task tool-call/output budgets and correlated logging on WorkItem.toolCalls.

tasks.name: Define Level 2 task and execution contracts
deliverables: Define versioned task input, acceptance-criteria, plan, patch, verification, approval, and final-result schemas
Define terminal statuses that distinguish completed, incomplete, blocked, denied, and failed work
Specify fail-closed behavior for missing context, invalid plans, unavailable checks, and malformed model output
Document the Level 2 boundary: scoped implementation with human review, not autonomous merge or deployment
Use one verification status vocabulary across contracts.js and verification-repair-loop.js
acceptanceCriteria: Schemas reject missing task descriptions and invalid acceptance criteria
Result states cannot mark unverified or scaffold-only output as completed
Contract fixtures cover valid, invalid, blocked, and failed cases
A real passing VerificationRepairLoop result satisfies validateCompletion
tasks.notes: Confirmed complete and tracking corrected on 2026-10-07 (tracking had incorrectly shown this task as PENDING after the work was finished). Not re-verified as part of P12-T003; if the earlier 'passed' vs 'pass' status-vocabulary note resurfaces, re-open and re-check contracts.js against verification-repair-loop.js.

tasks.name: Implement real model-backed agent step execution
deliverables: Replace WorkOrchestrator._executeStep stub with an injected executor interface
Pass the approved plan step, task contract, bounded context, and cancellation signal to the executor
Validate structured model output before accepting step results
Return explicit provider, timeout, cancellation, and malformed-output failures
acceptanceCriteria: A deterministic fake executor can run the orchestrator end-to-end without network access
No model provider is invoked unless explicitly configured
Execution failures never produce success-shaped step results

tasks.name: Connect ToolRegistry to agent execution
deliverables: Inject ToolRegistry into the execution context and expose only registered tools
Make tool schemas and outputs available to the model executor
Record tool name, validated arguments, result status, duration, and bounded output in the work log
Enforce per-task tool-call and output budgets
Do not expose execute_command to the model; replace it with an allowlisted check runner that takes check IDs, not shell text
Add a hash-guarded edit tool that rejects edits when the file changed since it was read
Replace the get_diagnostics stub with real linter diagnostics, or mark the tool unavailable
acceptanceCriteria: Agent execution can perform read/search/edit/check operations only through registered tools
Unknown tools, invalid arguments, budget exhaustion, and tool failures are explicit
Tool execution logs are correlated with task and plan-step IDs
No agent-reachable tool executes arbitrary model-supplied shell text
get_diagnostics never reports zero issues when diagnostics were not actually collected
tasks.notes: WorkOrchestrator now constructs a ToolRegistry by default and injects tools/toolSchemas into every step executor call; unknown tools and invalid arguments are rejected explicitly without invoking the registry; per-task tool-call and output budgets are enforced before execution and recorded on WorkItem.toolCalls correlated with itemId/taskId/stepId; execute_command was removed and replaced by an allowlisted run_check tool (checkId only: lint/typecheck/test/build, no shell text); edit_file enforces a sha256 content-hash guard against stale edits; get_diagnostics now runs the real LinterOrchestrator and reports available:false with a reason instead of fabricating zero issues when no linter is configured. Fixed a pre-existing reserved-word bug in permissions.js ('protected' used as a loop variable) that was surfaced when tool-registry.js began importing PermissionManager. Verification: all 38 focused tool-registry/orchestrator/pipeline-control tests pass; the broader 26-file run had 348 passing tests and 2 unrelated pre-existing failures (reproduced on the clean baseline); the full test runner hangs in an unrelated security-command recursion issue.

tasks.name: Build bounded repository context for coding tasks
deliverables: Use workspace search, file inspection, language detection, and available symbol analysis to gather relevant context
Honor explicit file scope, ignore rules, file-size caps, and token budgets
Track each context item by workspace-relative path and content hash
Report when requested files are missing, excluded, or truncated
acceptanceCriteria: Context collection stays within configured file-count and token limits
Absolute paths outside the workspace are rejected
Context provenance is available in the task result
tasks.notes: Implemented and wired bounded workspace context collection into WorkOrchestrator. It supports explicit file scopes and bounded search discovery, honors path exclusions and file/byte/token/search limits, detects language and common declared symbols, hashes context by workspace-relative path, and reports missing/excluded/truncated inputs. Context provenance is included in task results. Verification: 5 T004 tests and 20 related orchestrator/pipeline regression tests passed.

tasks.name: Generate and validate actionable execution plans
deliverables: Replace keyword-only plan steps with executor-produced structured plans grounded in gathered context
Require a bounded affected-file set, ordered steps, acceptance criteria, verification commands, and risks
Validate dependencies, workspace scope, step budgets, and approval requirements before execution
Persist the exact approved plan and its version with the work item
acceptanceCriteria: Plans with no actionable steps, unresolved dependencies, or unbounded scope are rejected
Plan validation is deterministic and covered by positive and negative tests
The approval view represents the exact plan that will execute
tasks.notes: Implemented executor-supported structured plans grounded in bounded gathered context, with deterministic fallback planning, explicit acceptance criteria, verification check IDs, workspace/scope/dependency/budget validation, and approval requirements. The work item persists the frozen plan, version, and approval digest. Verification: all 4 focused P12-T005 tests and 25 adjacent P12-T002/T003/T004 regressions passed.

tasks.name: Generate and apply reviewable workspace patches
deliverables: Replace CodeGenerator scaffold patches with model-generated structured create, modify, and delete operations
Apply patches through DiffReviewSystem rather than a new write path, extending it with content-hash expectations
Validate patch paths, content hashes, expected original content, and changed-file limits before applying
Produce a unified diff and per-file summary before approval or application
Reject empty, scaffold-only, malformed, conflicting, or stale patches
acceptanceCriteria: Patch application is workspace-contained and rejects traversal and symlink escape attempts
A stale source file causes a conflict result without overwriting user edits
No patch is reported as implemented until the intended content is actually present
Patch generation and application have isolated temporary-workspace tests
No patch is applied unless it belongs to an approved plan and passes the approval gate

tasks.name: Enforce action-level permissions and approval gates
deliverables: Replace WorkOrchestrator._checkPermissions with PermissionManager enforcement
Apply permission policy to each tool call and patch operation, not only to the initial plan
Require explicit approval for destructive edits, dependency changes, broad scope, and configured high-risk actions
Bind approval to the plan and patch digest and invalidate it if either changes
Ensure cancellation, denial, or approval timeout prevents subsequent writes
acceptanceCriteria: Denied and expired approvals result in zero workspace mutations
Any change to an approved plan or patch requires renewed approval
Policy decisions are auditable and tested against adversarial requests

tasks.name: Run real verification checks and report evidence
deliverables: Replace WorkOrchestrator._verifyWork stub with real configured test, lint, type-check, and build command execution
Run commands with bounded timeout, output size, environment, and workspace scope
Capture command, exit code, duration, and sanitized bounded output for each check
Distinguish passed, failed, skipped, unavailable, errored, and timed-out checks, extending VerificationRepairLoop states with a timeout state
acceptanceCriteria: A failed required check prevents task completion
A missing required check is not represented as passing
No check executes an implicit shell command supplied by model text
Verification evidence is included in the final work result

tasks.name: Add bounded verification-driven repair loop
deliverables: Connect the existing verification-repair loop to agent patches and check failures
Feed only relevant, bounded diagnostics back to the executor
Cap repair iterations, changed files, tokens, elapsed time, and model/tool cost
Stop and return a reviewable partial result when limits are reached or checks regress
acceptanceCriteria: Repair stops at configured limits and cannot silently reset its budgets
A repair cannot bypass the original permissions or approval digest
Tests cover fixed-on-retry, persistent failure, regression, cancellation, and limit exhaustion

tasks.name: Persist agent runs, checkpoints, and audit events
deliverables: Persist task contract, plan, approval, tool events, patch digests, verification evidence, and final status
Resume only from validated checkpoints and re-check workspace hashes before continuation
Redact credentials and sensitive file contents from persisted records
Expose stable history and status data to existing agent interfaces
acceptanceCriteria: A process restart does not convert incomplete work to completed
Tampered, incompatible, or stale checkpoints fail with an explicit recovery state
Persistence tests verify redaction and deterministic resume behavior

tasks.name: Expose supervised code-generation workflow consistently
deliverables: Expose start, plan review, approval, progress, cancellation, and result through CLI, HTTP API, and MCP
Return the same task ID, autonomy profile, approval state, patch summary, and verification evidence on each surface
Register Level 2 agent actions in the shared capability groups
Document non-interactive approval requirements and safe headless defaults
acceptanceCriteria: CLI, API, and MCP invoke the same application service and produce equivalent state transitions
Headless execution denies actions that require a human approver when no approval channel is configured
Interface contract tests cover successful, denied, cancelled, and failed work

tasks.name: Prove Level 2 behavior with end-to-end acceptance suite
deliverables: Create offline end-to-end tasks that modify a disposable repository and verify intended behavior
Cover new feature, bug fix, regression test, unsafe request, missing toolchain, failed check, and human denial
Assert resulting diffs, real check invocations, approval binding, persistence, and failure states
Publish operator guide, supported-provider matrix, known limitations, and Level 2 acceptance evidence
acceptanceCriteria: No fake executor, stub verifier, scaffold patch, or network dependency is used by core acceptance tests
Every success case proves the workspace changed as intended and all required checks passed
Every blocked or failed case proves unsafe changes were not left behind
Phase 12 exit requires all critical acceptance cases passing

exitCriteria: The agent can implement bounded tasks using real tools and apply validated, reviewable patches
Required checks execute for real and failures cannot be reported as successful work
Risky actions require plan- and patch-bound human approval
Changes, tool calls, and verification evidence are auditable and resumable
Level 2 end-to-end acceptance suite passes on supported operating systems
